title: Effective Faraday interaction between light and Helium-3 nuclear spins in a multi-pass cell
authors: Kaiwen Yi, Yida Sha, Zejia Lin, Matteo Fadel, Xiang Peng
abstract: Helium-3 nuclear spins form an exceptionally stable quantum system with extremely long coherence time, offering exciting opportunities for quantum technologies. In particular, nuclear spin-squeezed states promise enhanced precision for sensing tasks and tests of new physics. A central challenge for all these applications is the realization of a controllable light-nuclear spin interface. Here we experimentally demonstrate such an interface by exploiting metastability-exchange collisions in a low-pressure helium-3 gas cell at room temperature. A radio-frequency discharge produces a small population of metastable atoms that both enables efficient optical pumping and mediates an effective Faraday interaction between the collective nuclear spin and an optical probe. We quantitatively characterize the strength of this interaction as a function of the nuclear polarization, applied magnetic field, and probe-beam parameters. Moreover, we show that using a multi-pass cell enhances this interaction by effectively increasing the optical depth. Extrapolating to a tenfold increase of the probe power used in the present experiment, we project a measurement-induced squeezing rate of 0.52 s$^{-1}$. Our results provide a practical pathway for optical access to helium-3 nuclear spins and open prospects for generating long-lived, macroscopic nuclear spin-squeezed states for quantum metrology.
summary: The researchers demonstrated an effective Faraday interaction between light and Helium-3 nuclear spins using metastable atoms generated in a multi-pass gas cell. By quantifying this interaction, they established a practical method for optically accessing these long-lived quantum memories. This paves the way for generating highly entangled, spin-squeezed states for advanced quantum sensing.
main_problem: The central goal is to realize and quantify a controllable light-nuclear spin interface for Helium-3 nuclear spins, which is crucial for advancing quantum metrology applications like generating spin-squeezed states.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated an effective Faraday interaction mediated by metastability-exchange collisions (MECs) in a multi-pass cell. They projected achieving a measurement-induced squeezing rate of $0.52 	ext{ s}^{-1}$ with increased probe power.
method: The experiment uses optical pumping and measures the resulting spin dynamics via Free Induction Decay (FID) signals, comparing single-pass versus enhanced multi-pass cell geometries to characterize the coupling strength $\Omega(i)$.
model_or_system: The system involves ${}^3	ext{He}$ gas at room temperature, where metastable atoms generated by an RF discharge mediate a Faraday interaction between the light probe and the ground-state nuclear spin. The theoretical framework models this using effective Hamiltonians derived from atomic level structures.
key_observables: Effective coupling strength $\Omega(i)$, Free Induction Decay (FID) signal amplitude, Nuclear polarization ($M$), and Metastable density ($\langle n_m angle$).
important_parameters: Nuclear polarization ($M$), applied magnetic field ($B$), probe beam power ($	ext{PL}$), optical depth enhancement via multi-pass cells, and the ratio of coupling constants ($\chi$ vs. $\eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as weak Faraday coupling, short MEC times relative to Larmor periods, and quasi-static nuclear polarization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (multi-pass cell), the dependence of the effective coupling strength $\Omega(i)$ on magnetic field and probe power, and time traces showing the switchability of the interaction by controlling the RF discharge power.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the fundamental physical mechanism (MECs mediating Faraday interaction) to detailed measurements of key parameters like metastable density and polarization. It then systematically compares single-pass vs. multi-pass cell results, culminating in demonstrating the scalability towards high squeezing rates.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally validated pathway for coupling light fields directly to nuclear spins—a notoriously difficult task due to long coherence times but weak optical coupling—making it highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems research.
